### Observed differences

- Activity A01 occurred exactly once in every trace in the earlier window (participation 100 in 100 traces, mean 1.0 occurrence per trace, typically around two-thirds of the way through each trace); in the later window it is not observed in any of the 200 traces. [OCC001, POS001]
- In the earlier window A01 was embedded between A05 and A07: about 51 in 100 of A05's outgoing transitions led to A01, and about 99 in 100 of A01's transitions led to A07; A01 also cooccurred with A02, A03, A04 and A07 in essentially every trace. In the later window A05 leads directly to A07 (about 49 in 100 of its transitions), A01 shows no outgoing transitions, and every pair involving A01 changed from (near-)always occurring together to the partner appearing alone — for example A01–A05 went from cooccurrence in all traces to A05-only in all traces, and A01–A06 from cooccurrence in 45 in 100 traces to A06-only in 44 and neither in 57. [DIR004, DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- Following distances between the remaining activities shortened by one step, as expected if each trace became one event shorter: A02→A03 from lag 5 to 4, A02→A07 from 4 to 3, A04→A03 from 4 to 3, A05→A03 from 3 to 2, A05→A07 from 2 to 1, A06→A07 from 3 to 2, and A06→A03 from 4 to 3. [LAG001, LAG005, LAG006, LAG010, LAG014, LAG015, LAG019]
- Relative event positions shifted consistently with the shorter traces: A04, A05 and A06 now occur slightly later (medians 0.20→0.25, 0.40→0.50, 0.43→0.50) while A07 occurs slightly earlier (0.80→0.75). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Smaller residual shifts remain: A04's outgoing share to A05 fell from about 92 to 87 in 100 while its shares to A07 (about 2→7), A06 (2→4) and A03 (1→3) rose, and A02's split between A04 and A05 moved from about 90/10 to 87/13. Pairs and distances not involving A01 stayed essentially the same. [DIR003, DIR002, REL007, REL009, REL013, LAG020]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the step performed by A01 was dropped from the traces: A01, which previously ran exactly once per trace between A05 and A07, is no longer observed, and A05 now leads directly to A07 where it previously led to A01 in about half of its transitions. Both elements are observed directly — the disappearance (participation 100 in 100 traces before, 0 in 100 after, on 200 traces per window) and the rewiring (A05's successor profile shifting from A01 at 51 in 100 to A07 at 49 in 100) — and all six relational pairs with A01 together with seven following-distance items change in exactly the pattern expected when a single event is removed from every trace. [OCC001, DIR004, DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG001, LAG005, LAG006, LAG010, LAG014, LAG015, LAG019]

Limitations: zero participation only shows that A01 was not recorded in the later window, so the evidence cannot distinguish a genuine removal of the step from A01 still being executed but no longer logged, nor say anything about why the step disappeared. No screening baseline is provided, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with a chance expectation; the judgement rests on the directness and consistency of the items, which a single underlying difference explains throughout. [OCC001, DIR004]

Other differences: A04 now routes somewhat less often to A05 and more often to A07, A06 and A03 (for example A05 at 92 vs 87, A07 at 2 vs 7 in 100 outgoing transitions), and A02 slightly more often to A05 than to A04 (about 10.5 vs 13.5 in 100); these shifts are small, and the evidence cannot show whether they are rerouting around the missing A01 or sampling variation. [DIR003, DIR002]
